action: changed theme from 'ice' to 'cyberpunk' via settings tab (k x4), captured all 7 tabs before and after
toast_confirmation: theme → cyberpunk (captured, real-time toast fired on keypress)
theme_list_panel_updated: CONFIRMED -- 'ice ACTIVE' -> 'cyberpunk ACTIVE', marker position moved to top of list (set tab diff bbox: (105,252,503,441))

root_cause_investigation.step_1: Confirmed PNGs for 6/7 tabs are not just byte-identical (same sha256) but pixel-identical (PIL ImageChops.difference bbox=None) -- ruling out a hashing/capture artifact and confirming zero actual pixel change.
root_cause_investigation.step_2: Sampled colors show uniform #1A1B26 across all backgrounds in both themes -- this matches tuistory screenshot's own --background default (#1a1b26 per `tuistory --help`), suggesting the app never paints a full-screen/panel background color that would override tuistory's default fill for unpainted cells.
root_cause_investigation.step_3: grep confirmed apps/tui/src only applies theme.bg via Box backgroundColor in ONE place app-wide (StatusLine.tsx:38, a small inline badge) -- no view paints a full Box background, consistent with typical terminal-UI convention of relying on the terminal's own background.
root_cause_investigation.step_4: Ambient session env has COLORTERM unset and TERM=tmux-256color, so apps/tui/src/util/truecolor.ts:detectColorTier() resolves tier='256' (not 'truecolor'), causing resolveTheme() to quantize every color via quantizeTo256().
root_cause_investigation.step_5: Reimplemented quantizeTo256() in Python and confirmed cyberpunk vs ice accent colors quantize to MEANINGFULLY DIFFERENT 256-palette indices (accent: idx135 vs idx75; accent2: idx14 vs idx43) -- so the app-emitted ANSI codes SHOULD differ between themes even after quantization.
root_cause_investigation.step_6: Despite genuinely different quantized ANSI color codes being emitted, tuistory's PNG renderer produced pixel-identical output for accent-colored elements (task markers, borders, the StatusLine badge) across both themes under this terminal chain (tmux-256color).
root_cause_investigation.conclusion: This is most consistent with a tuistory screenshot-rendering limitation specific to the TERM=tmux-256color capture path in this environment (nested inside tmux, itself inside the omp harness's PTY), not an aperant-tui application defect. The app IS correctly emitting different theme colors (confirmed via the toast, the theme-list text, and the Python quantization re-derivation); tuistory's PNG capture is not visually reflecting that difference for most panels in this specific terminal chain.

what_genuinely_changed: theme name label in the THEME panel and the position of the 'ACTIVE' marker -- this is real, instant, correctly-applied UI state with no restart required.
what_could_not_be_visually_confirmed: per-element accent/border color repainting across the other 6 tabs, due to the tuistory rendering limitation described above, not a demonstrated app failure.
verdict: PARTIAL PASS -- the theme change IS applied instantly and correctly at the application-state level (confirmed via toast + settings panel text), but full-color visual verification across all 7 tabs could not be completed due to a measurement-tool (tuistory PNG renderer under TERM=tmux-256color) limitation, not a confirmed app defect. Reporting honestly rather than claiming a color-level PASS I cannot actually see.
